newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran, Germany's West LB in oilfield financing - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Germany's West LB in oilfield financing - MEES.

text.p: The National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) has signed preliminary documents for a $160 million loan being arranged by Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank (West LB) for the development of the Soroush oilfield, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) said on Monday.

The newsletter said this was despite heightened political tension between Iran and Germany. But it added that the loan was approved "immediately prior" to the April 10 verdict by a German court that Iran's leaders ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin in 1992.
The loan is being arranged by West LB on behalf of the Iranian Offshore Engineering Construction Co (IOEC), which won the development contract on the Soroush offshore field earlier this year.
IOEC is 51 percent owned by NIOC and 49 percent by Iran's Ministry of Industry.

"Repayment of the IOEC loan is to be realised through the assignment of funds from NIOC's existing crude oil export contracts rather than from the sale of output from the Soroush field itself, making agreement on the part of NIOC a crucial element of the project's financing structure."
But MEES said the financing facility was far from finalised.
"West LB must now return to the other banks which are participating in the syndication in order to secure their agreement on the renegotiated terms and conditions," MEES said.
It said IOEC has other financing options if the participating banks do not agree to NIOC conditions, or withdraw from the project for political reasons.
